hook.line: Vale's biggest conditions use the most ordinary verbs: be, go, know, be there. Those are exactly the verbs that break the pattern, so they get their own short list.
hook.en: I want you to be honest with me. (to a friend, a man)

examples.es: Necesito que vayas al banco hoy.
examples.en: I need you to go to the bank today. (to a friend)
I want you to know something, Tomás.

examples.es: Quiero que el café sea de los dos.
examples.en: I want the café to belong to both of us.
Hernando wants us to be calm.

examples.es: Necesito que me des una respuesta hoy.
examples.en: I need you to give me an answer today. (to a friend)

examples.es: Quiero que haya café para todos.
examples.en: I want there to be coffee for everyone.
I don't want you to have problems. (to a friend)

rule:
Most wish forms come straight from the I form, the way your *usted* commands do:
*tengo*: *tenga*
*hago*: *haga*
*digo*: *diga*
*salgo*: *salga*
*conozco*: *conozca*

Six verbs can't do that, because their I form doesn't end in *-o*: *soy*, *voy*, *estoy*, *sé*, *doy*, *he*. Learn their wish forms as a set:

*ser*: *sea*
*ir*: *vaya*
*estar*: *esté*
*saber*: *sepa*
*dar*: *dé*
*haber* (there is): *haya*

After that they behave: *seas*, *sea*, *seamos*, *sean*. *Esté* keeps its accent in every person except we: *estés*, *estemos*, *estén*. *Dé* has an accent only so you don't confuse it with *de* (of). *Haya* has just the one form: *Quiero que haya café.*
smallPrint: Teachers call these the irregular present subjunctive forms.

options: I need you to go to the bank.
I need you to be at the bank.
I need to go to the bank.

readAndPick.es: Quiero que estés aquí el lunes.
options: I want you to go there on Monday.
I want you to be here on Monday.
I want to be here on Monday.

readAndPick.es: No quiero que Altamira sepa nada.
options: I don't want Altamira to know anything.
I don't want to know anything about Altamira.
Altamira doesn't want me to know anything.

readAndPick.es: Quiero que haya café para todos.
options: I want to have coffee with everyone.
I want there to be coffee for everyone.

readAndPick.es: Quiero que me des la llave.
options: I want to give you the key.
I want you to give me the key.
We want to be on time.
They want us to be on time.
We want them to be on time.
Do you want to go with me?
Do you want me to go with you?

readAndPick.es: Quiero que estemos juntos en esto.
options: I want us to be in this together.
I want you to be in this together.

readAndPick.es: Necesito que me digas la verdad.
options: I need to tell you the truth.
I need you to tell me the truth.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *eres* or *seas* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *Quiero que ___ honesto conmigo.* (I want you to be honest with me.)
yourTurn.why: After *quiero que*, *ser* becomes *sea*, and for you, *seas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *vas* or *vayas* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *No quiero que ___ solo.* (I don't want you to go alone.)
yourTurn.why: *Ir* turns into *vaya* when you want someone to go: *vayas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a friend: I need you to give me the key.
yourTurn.answer: Necesito que me des la llave.
yourTurn.why: *Dar* becomes *dé*, and for you it's *des*, no accent needed.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a friend: I want you to know something.
yourTurn.why: *Saber* has its own wish form: *sepa*, so *sepas* for you.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I want there to be coffee for everyone.
yourTurn.answer: Quiero que haya café para todos.
yourTurn.why: There is is *hay*, and the wish form is *haya*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about you all (a group): *Necesito que estés aquí a las siete.*
yourTurn.answer: Necesito que estén aquí a las siete.
yourTurn.why: For you all, add *n*, and the accent stays: *estén*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal, to Hernando (*usted*): *Quiero que me digas la verdad.*
yourTurn.answer: Quiero que me diga la verdad.
yourTurn.why: For *usted*, drop the *s*: *diga*, the same as the command.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Quiero que tengas problemas.* Then it finally sounds kind.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Eres* states a fact; what you want someone to be is *seas*.
*Ir* has its own wish form, *vaya*, so for you it's *vayas*.

pitfalls.wrong: Quiero que me de la llave.
pitfalls.right: Quiero que me dé la llave.
pitfalls.why: Without the accent, *de* means of. The verb is *dé*.

personal: Write one sentence about something you want for someone you care about, using *sea*, *esté*, *vaya* or *sepa*. For example, what you want your best friend to know.
